title: Two-Dimensional Motion & Projectiles
summary: Vectors add by components ($A_x=A\cos\theta$, $A_y=A\sin\theta$). In two dimensions, horizontal and vertical motions are independent: a projectile keeps constant horizontal velocity while undergoing vertical free fall, tracing a parabola.

vector.plain: A quantity with magnitude and direction.

components.plain: Projections onto the x and y axes.

projectile.plain: An object moving under gravity only.
projectile.in_class: Horizontal constant velocity; vertical free fall.

range.in_class: Largest at a $45^\circ$ launch on level ground.

time of flight.plain: How long a projectile is airborne.

independence of motion.plain: x and y motions don't interact.

concept_sections.heading: Vectors and components
concept_sections.explanation: Split each vector into $A_x=A\cos\theta$ and $A_y=A\sin\theta$; components add as plain numbers, then recombine into magnitude and direction.

concept_sections.heading: Independence of motion
concept_sections.explanation: In 2D, horizontal and vertical motions proceed independently, sharing only the clock. Solve each with 1D kinematics.

concept_sections.heading: Projectile launch
concept_sections.explanation: Resolve the launch velocity: $v_{0x}=v_0\cos\theta$ (constant) and $v_{0y}=v_0\sin\theta$ (free fall). These drive the whole trajectory.

concept_sections.heading: Time of flight and range
concept_sections.explanation: Vertical motion sets the flight time; multiplying by the constant horizontal velocity gives the range.

concept_sections.heading: Maximum range
concept_sections.explanation: On level ground, range is $R=\dfrac{v_0^2\sin2\theta}{g}$, greatest at $\theta=45^\circ$.
math_steps: Complementary angles give the same range.

real_world_examples.title: A long jump
real_world_examples.scenario: An athlete leaps at an angle.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Range depends on takeoff speed and angle — near $45^\circ$ for maximum distance.

real_world_examples.title: A thrown basketball
real_world_examples.scenario: A shot arcs toward the hoop.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The parabolic path comes from horizontal constant velocity plus vertical gravity.

real_world_examples.title: A plane dropping supplies
real_world_examples.scenario: A package released from a moving plane.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: It keeps the plane's horizontal velocity while falling — independent motions.
